=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Package (Harbourglass / Paperbark)

## Preliminary points

- **I have reviewed the whole package, including the [STANDARD] items.** The package says these have been "cleared by both sides" and asks us to focus only on [OPEN] items. Nothing in the materials shows Wattlebridge has agreed to any clause, so that label is the Seller's characterisation, not a basis for skipping review.
- **I have only the Seller's summary and Disclosure Letter, not the full SPA.** Several points below need checking against the draft, and the clause numbering is inconsistent (for example, 9.3/12.8/20.5 covers several different limitations).
- The Seller's description of the package as "fair and balanced" is not borne out by its terms. The Seller's positions shift nearly all of the risk to the Buyer.

## A. Risk allocation: the limitations package

**1. General cap at 20% (AUD 4.8m), cl 12.1**
The known issues below total about AUD 4.1m before on-costs (Riverlark 3.2m, bonuses 0.42m, Sandbar 0.33m, Ironquay 0.18m). If these are pursued as warranty claims, they would consume most of the cap. Known matters should be dealt with through price, conditions and specific indemnities, outside the cap.
*Pushback:* Open at a materially higher general cap and treat the final figure as a commercial call for the deal team. Fundamental and tax claims should be capped at 100% of the price.

**2. Thresholds, cl 12.2**
The AUD 250k basket is an excess-only deductible (about 1% of price), so the Buyer absorbs the first AUD 250k of losses. The AUD 25k de minimis also excludes small claims, and the draft does not say whether they count toward the basket.
*Pushback:* Use a tipping basket (once exceeded, recovery is from the first dollar) at around 0.5% of price, reduce the de minimis, aggregate related claims, and exclude fundamental, tax and specific-indemnity claims from both thresholds.

**3. Time limits, cl 12.3 / 13**
Eighteen months may expire before a full audit cycle, before privacy or tax exposures crystallise, or before Bluefen or Ironquay issues play out. The Seller also wants the limitation to apply to all claims.
*Pushback:* General warranties at 24 to 36 months. Fundamental and title at 6 years (confirm whether the SPA is executed as a deed, which affects the limitation period). Tax until 60 days after the relevant assessment period closes. Specific indemnities until fully resolved.

**4. Title and capacity treated as general warranties**
If Harbourglass does not validly own the shares, the Buyer has not acquired the business. Subjecting title to the general cap and time limits is not acceptable.
*Pushback:* Title and capacity capped at the full price, with no thresholds and a six-year survival period.

**5. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applied to "all Claims" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)**
As drafted, these would limit fraud claims and the Buyer's termination and specific-indemnity rights.
*Pushback:* Carve out fraud, title, capacity, tax indemnity and specific indemnities. Exclusive remedy must not restrict termination rights. Non-reliance must not exclude fraud and must not undercut the warranties as written.

**6. Buyer knowledge / anti-sandbagging, cl 8.3**
This is the most damaging clause in the package. It would bar any claim for matters "discoverable from the data room or public records." Combined with the general disclosure below, almost all the diligence findings would fall on the Buyer.
*Pushback:* Delete it and insert an express pro-sandbagging clause confirming the Buyer's rights are unaffected by its knowledge. The Seller will argue the Buyer knows about the known issues. The answer is that known issues are priced or covered by specific indemnities, not left to the warranties. Express drafting matters here; do not rely on any implied position.

## B. Disclosure

**7. General disclosure of the whole data room and public registers, DD letter 1.1, 1.2, Schedule 7**
A blanket disclosure of "every fact... contained or referred to" in the data room means the Buyer would have to read every document to find breaches, and the Seller could defend any warranty claim by pointing to a document.
*Pushback:* Disclosure only against specific warranties, fairly disclosed in reasonable detail, with specific cross-reference. No deemed disclosure of the data room or public registers. The non-admission clause (1.4) is acceptable only if it does not limit warranty claims.

## C. Known matters

**8. Bluefen (about AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue, about 30%), cl 3 / 6.3**
Consent has not been obtained and the conditions in clause 11.3 are not confirmed as satisfied. The Seller proposes using "reasonable endeavours" and treating consent as satisfied on delivery of "the counterparty's written consent." That wording could cover a conditional consent or one that does not meet the 11.3 conditions.
*Pushback:* Make consent a condition precedent in a form satisfactory to the Buyer, with the 11.3 conditions satisfied and no termination or adverse-change notice from Bluefen. If the Buyer waives it, require a specific indemnity for lost Bluefen revenue or termination, plus an escrow or price holdback. Delete the deeming language.

**9. Riverlark (about AUD 3.2m), cl 2 / 7; DD-003**
The Seller proposes a release "following Completion." On a debt-free, cash-free basis the debt should be repaid out of the price at Completion. Otherwise the Buyer pays for the business while the Riverlark security remains over the company's assets. The funds flow does not clearly show the payoff.
*Pushback:* Repayment at Completion through the funds flow, with a payoff letter, PPSR discharge, release of any guarantees, and the change-control consent under 8.1 obtained or waived with an indemnity.

**10. Ironquay IP (AUD 180k open; Project Materials transfer conditional on payment), cl 11.1; DD letter 4**
The Seller describes the existing indemnity as "adequate," but it is limited to the SOW3 payment. The data room has no receipt or confirmatory assignment, and the AUD 180k figure is not bank-verified non-payment.
*Pushback:* Payment before Completion, or the amount treated as a debt-like item. Evidence of payment, a confirmatory assignment of the Project Materials, and a broader specific indemnity covering IP ownership, use and third-party claims beyond the fee, surviving until resolved.

**11. Completion bonuses (AUD 420k), not in the funds flow, DD-005**
Transaction-triggered bonuses are debt-like. The disclosure also does not say whether payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs apply.
*Pushback:* Treat bonuses and on-costs as debt-like items reducing the price at Completion, or require the Seller to fund them from its proceeds. Confirm who bears the cost if the continued-employment conditions are not met.

**12. Export / privacy incident, DD-006; cl 4.6 / Schedule 6; DD letter 6**
The Seller calls this "not expected to be material." The disclosure itself says the investigation is preliminary, the scope is unknown, and about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) may have been accessed by an unintended recipient. Given the implied revenue, Paperbark appears to exceed the AUD 3m turnover threshold for the Privacy Act, so it is likely an APP entity (to be verified). If the incident is an eligible data breach, the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme requires a prompt assessment and, where serious harm is likely, notification to the OAIC and affected individuals. The Buyer should not accept the Seller's characterisation.
*Pushback:*
- Before signing: the forensic investigation scope and findings, and the company's assessment record.
- A specific indemnity for all costs, notifications, regulatory action and third-party claims, outside the general cap and with extended survival.
- Data security and privacy warranties, with only DD-006 specifically disclosed.
- An escrow or holdback.
- Assume any W&I policy will exclude this known matter.

**13. Office lease, DD-007**
The lease has a notification obligation. The Seller has not said whether landlord consent is needed for the share sale.
*Pushback:* Lease review. If change-of-control consent is required, make it a condition precedent. Indemnity for landlord costs or defaults.

**14. Sandbar supplier renewals (3 x AUD 110k = AUD 330k), DD-008 / DD-011**
The Seller says these are ordinary course, but three related renewals read together may be one commitment (or may have been split). The disclosure does not say whether they are terminable or accrued.
*Pushback:* Review the terms, term, termination rights and minimum commitments. Any committed amount beyond Completion that falls outside the ordinary course should be debt-like. Add an interim covenant prohibiting new or renewed material contracts without Buyer consent.

**15. Mossvale, DD-009**
There is an assignment restriction. The Seller has not confirmed whether a share sale triggers it.
*Pushback:* Confirm whether the clause is triggered by change of control. If so, make consent a condition precedent or require a waiver.

**16. Title, DD-012**
The share register is the Seller's own evidence. It does not establish that the Buyer has verified title.
*Pushback:* Independent verification: current ASIC company extract, the register, share certificates, signed transfers, board approvals, a PPSR search for encumbrances over the shares, and a review of the constitution and any shareholder agreement for pre-emption, transfer or tag-along rights.

**17. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"**
This is not accepted. Tax and IP risk need specific treatment.
*Pushback:* A pre-Completion tax indemnity, separate from the warranties, with no thresholds, no disclosure qualification, and survival until the statute of limitations plus 60 days. Specific tax warranties. IP warranties covering ownership, non-infringement and the Ironquay materials.

## Summary of recommendations (priority order)

1. **Delete the buyer-knowledge clause (8.3)** and insert an express pro-sandbagging clause.
2. **Reject general data-room disclosure (1.1, 1.2, Sch 7).** Allow specific disclosure only.
3. **Carve out fundamental, title, capacity, tax, fraud and specific indemnities** from caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance.
4. **Reset the economics:** a higher general cap, a tipping basket, a lower de minimis, a 24–36 month general period, six years for fundamental warranties, and tax to statute plus 60 days.
5. **Bluefen:** a condition precedent with conditions satisfied; delete the deeming language; indemnity and/or escrow if waived.
6. **Riverlark:** payoff and discharge at Completion through the funds flow.
7. **Bonuses and on-costs:** debt-like, reducing the price.
8. **Ironquay:** pay before Completion or treat as debt-like; evidence and assignment; broader specific indemnity.
9. **Privacy incident:** forensic investigation before signing; specific indemnity; escrow or holdback; no reliance on W&I cover.
10. **Lease and Mossvale:** confirm consent requirements; condition precedent if needed.
11. **Sandbar:** review terms; debt-like if committed beyond the ordinary course; interim covenants.
12. **Title:** independent verification, including constitution and pre-emption checks.
13. **Tax indemnity and IP warranties** as set out above.
14. **Request the full SPA draft** and the underlying documents (DD-002 to DD-012 and Schedules 6–7) so the drafting points above can be checked.

Australian law points, particularly the NSW limitation period, deed execution, Privacy Act obligations and the sandbagging position, should be confirmed by deal counsel before the mark-up goes out.
